newsitem.title: USA: Utilities seek to stop some TVA power sales.
newsitem.headline: Utilities seek to stop some TVA power sales.

text.p: Five southern utilities Thursday asked a U.S. district court judge to order the Tennessee Valley Authority to stop selling power through East Kentucky Power Cooperative to customers outside TVA's area.
The court plans to hold a hearing on the request July 29, said a spokesman for Southern Co.

The filing followed up on a lawsuit the utilities launched last April in Birmingham, Alabama, alleging that TVA was selling electricity in sham deals to East Kentucky Power Cooperative, then physically delivering that power to other parties whom TVA is not allowed to supply.
The power agency denied the charges, a TVA spokesman said, adding that company officials had not yet seen the request for the court to bar the sales while the lawsuit proceeded.

The utilities -- Southern Co's Alabama Power, Georgia Power and Mississippi Power, Entergy Corp's Entergy Mississippi, and Duke Power Co -- said TVA should be stopped because it was "contaminating the market, it's hurting business," said Buddy Eller, Southern's Washington spokesman.
"East Kentucky Power Cooperative cannot physically take on its transmission system the amount of power which is supposedly being 'exchanged' by TVA," the utilities said.

The companies are concerned that TVA, which sells cheap power to the utilities, is starting to sell that same cheap electricity directly to other customers, taking away the utilities' sales advantage, an industry official said.
